title: Tin whistle
reference_instrument: a different whistle, for its held sound only and with no count: a Sweetone D tin whistle playing a slurred D major scale, cut between the slurs (Mirjam Plas, Escola Superior de Musica de Catalunya, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0). It is not the modelled Clare whistle, and no note of it stands alone
summary: Nothing here is graded: no licensed whistle recording is in the library, and the clip beside each note is a different whistle's slurred scale. Six of the eight notes sound flat of their names on the scale, by 21 to 35 c, from a pull the model doesn't explain, while D5 and D6 sit 3 and 7 c sharp; the harmonics don't follow the real one's. This is a Clare D whistle built from the ISVR measurements of one real whistle (Davies, Pinho and English 2006): bore, six finger holes, flue, window and pocket, blown at each note's printed air flow through a forced Bickley jet. It carries Fletcher's 1976 jet spreading as a trial, breath noise, and a labium offset borrowed from the recorder. D6 alone also has the jet swing limit. It models the paper's metered-air rig, not a player: the bore holds breath, but each note's mouth pressure comes from the paper's dry-air flow, and there is no tonguing, breath or finger motion.
physics_present: fs-couple flue_loop: a forced Bickley jet driven by a mouth pressure computed from each note's printed air flow through the card's windway law, with the 1.48 mm flue, acting on a connected duct network

The bore and six finger holes from the same paper, open or closed per its fingering chart, with the open holes' inner radiation matched in series, and the closed pocket behind the flue. The bore's open end reacts as an unflanged thin-walled tube (Garcia Mayen 2021, Eq. 14, via Silva et al. 2009), heard as a baffled monopole

The window's acoustic mass from its own 3-D wall cut, and its radiation from the outer face of the head's cylinder, that radiation's memory stepped exactly with the flow held over each step (27631e7a4)
The contraction loss at the flue exit (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I, vena-contracta coefficient 0.6)
Jet spreading by Fletcher 1976, a trial here: this flue is outside its measured 0.25 to 1.0 mm
A labium offset of 0.203 mm, 0.1374 flue heights, borrowed from the recorder (Bouterse 2010), because no printed whistle value was found. It gives the even harmonics a level at all
Breath noise at the window edge (Verge 1995): gain 1.3e-3 of the jet's dynamic pressure, opening at a flue Reynolds number of 700 (p. 196), through an order-two Butterworth band-pass

On D6 only, a limit on how far the jet can swing: Fletcher 1976's envelope, applied in time this model's own way. It lets the first harmonic lead on that note. On D5, G5 and B5 it makes the match worse, so it stays off

In the bore, the player's breath (the shared woodwind pack: Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969, Fletcher and Rossing sec. 8.1, saturated at 27 C with 4.5 % CO2 and 16.5 % O2 dry), with gas-derived viscothermal loss on the bore's 7 sections, its memory stepped exactly with the flow held over each step (adbb97dbb and f78078db2); the room's dry air at 20 C outside the bore, and Stokes-Kirchhoff air along the path to the receiver
A physical receiver 1 m above the window, summing every open aperture, with the compact radiation load declared valid to 2.8 kHz
physics_missing: A graded comparison: the clip beside each note is a Sweetone D whistle's slurred scale, cut between the slurs, so only its held sound compares, with no count. A second whistle's scale differs from it by 3 to 17 dB on single harmonics, so one recording doesn't fix a target closer than that

Pitch: on the scale the notes read D5 +3, E5 -23, F#5 -35, G5 -24, A5 -31, B5 -21, C#6 -25 and D6 +7 c. On earlier renders, before the unflanged end and the breath, a scratch model with no jet put the passive modes of D5, G5, B5 and D6 18 to 48 c above where the renders sounded with wall loss on, so the jet pulled the notes flat; that model was not redone. No pressure was chosen to correct it

The real whistle's spectrum: on D5, G5 and B5, H2 is 31 to 35 dB under H1, against 17 to 25 on this whistle, and H5 stands 15 to 33 dB over it. On D6, H3 is -3.4 dB re H1 against -27, and H2 stands well over this whistle's

A jet drive from print that works here. Refused on these notes: the Auvray 2014 jet drive (wrong note on 10 of 11 whistle notes), the Ernoult-Fabre window mass, the unsteady windway with the forced jet, and the de la Cuadra 2005 exit law, whose Reynolds range excludes this flue. The momentum drive of Thwaites and Fletcher 1983 silences B5 and D6 and moves G5 to its third mode
A player: no tonguing, breath or finger motion. The bore holds breath, but each note's mouth pressure comes from the paper's dry-air flow and is not recomputed for breath
Attack and release: only the held sound can be compared. In the scale each note's output reaches digital silence 0.14 to 0.19 s after its release starts, so nothing rings beyond that
Overblown notes: none are posted. Only the paper's measured operating points were rendered, so where each register begins and any hysteresis are unmapped
Pages for E5, F#5, A5 and C#6: they appear only in the scale and melody, on cards with the same edits as the posted four, without the swing limit

The flue's true taper, the pocket's shape, the thin hole wall, hole shape and undercut, and the bore's narrowing at the wedge. Where the wedge tip sits in the wall isn't published, and the cards use one end of that bracket
A measured jet card: these cards use the repository's interim one

Openings that hear each other: the open holes and the end radiate apart. Tried with every opening hearing every other free-field, after the travel time between them (`outlet_mutual free-field`), which is passive here because the side holes carry baffled loads, the row lowered B5, D6 and G5 by 1.74, 0.13 and 1.81 c on the raw renders. All three already sit flat of the recording (16.2, 1.41 and 42.5 c), so the gap grew, to 17.9, 1.54 and 44.3 c. The mean miss of H2 to H12 re H1 against the recording's held part moved 7.85 to 7.81 dB on B5, 15.105 to 15.114 on D6 and 11.39 to 11.12 on G5. Weighted instead by the two openings' own radiation resistances (`outlet_mutual pritchard`, Pritchard 1960 as printed by Butler 2022, Eq. 1, as the flute's D4 and G4 pages carry it) and rendered on one binary, each page beside its own card without the row (2026-11-10), B5, D6 and G5 fell 3.54, 0.18 and 3.56 c and played 0.331, 0.020 and 0.385 dB quieter, so the gap grew again, to 19.7, 1.59 and 46.1 c, and the mean miss moved 7.85 to 7.71 dB on B5, 15.111 to 15.215 on D6 and 11.39 to 10.89 on G5. The pages and the scale and melody stops keep the openings apart; D5, with only the end open, has nothing to pair

Separated flow at the openings: the flow leaving each open hole and the open end separates and loses its kinetic energy, a loss in series with each opening's own radiation (`opening_losses`, Δp = ρQ|Q|/(2(C_c A)²)). Tried with C_c 1 on every opening: the open end as Atig, Dalmont and Gilbert 2004 print it (C. R. Mécanique 332:299-304, Eq. 3, c_d = 2 for a thin-walled unflanged end), the side holes at the row's ceiling of 1, a loss 1.2 times the one Dalmont et al. 2002 print for a sharp-edged hole (Acta Acust. united Ac. 88:567-575, K_h = 0.5, as quoted by Szwarcberg et al. 2024, JASA, Sec. III.2.1, which is C_c 1.096): a C_c above 1 would be pressure recovery, which this row's full-head loss cannot represent. Every page rendered. The row lowered B5, D5, D6 and G5 by 1.13, 0.08, 0.07 and 0.25 c on the raw renders. All four already sit flat of the recording (16.2, 19.9, 1.41 and 42.5 c), so the gap grew, to 17.3, 20.0, 1.48 and 42.8 c. The mean miss of H2 to H12 re H1 against the recording's held part moved 7.85 to 7.32 dB on B5, 10.00 to 9.77 on D5, 15.11 to 15.25 on D6 and 11.39 to 10.62 on G5. No page gains on both, so the row stays off

The player's airway (`upstream_airway`, the row the flute's C5, D4 and G4 pages carry): tried on all four pages, each beside its live card on one binary. The lungs supply the paper's blowing pressure plus the airway's steady drop (3.60 to 5.87 % of it), so the developing windway, judged again at that foot pressure, holds the paper's pressure, within 0.0004 Pa of the live page's. The pitch gap to the recording grew on every page, by 0.06 to 0.17 c, so no page carries the row. Its airway is Weibel's tree (Saab et al. 2021, Story 2008) with the voice cards' stand-in wall
